tool_args.old_string: Our study has several limiting assumptions that future work should address. First, all experiments use a single world-model architecture (DreamerV3's RSSM with discrete latents); while the CIVO mechanism---co-adaptation between learned temporal embeddings and the dynamics model---is architecturally general in principle, we have not verified whether it manifests in transformer-based world models \citep{micheli2023iris}, TD-MPC variants \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2}, or diffusion-based planners. Second, the primary evaluation covers two proprioceptive locomotion environments (Walker Walk and Cheetah Run) and one simulated manipulation task (PickCube); generalization to pixel-based observations, Atari, or real-robot deployments remains untested. Third, our causal claims rest on a factorial observational design rather than a formal causal identification strategy; confounds between embedding training dynamics and other optimizer state cannot be fully excluded. Fourth, the NVE $\geq 2.0\times$ threshold achieves perfect classification on our $n{=}36$ configurations but has not been validated on held-out architectures or environment families beyond our test suite. Finally, per-configuration seed counts (4--5 seeds; \citet{colas2018seeds}) are powered to detect the large-magnitude CIVO phenomenon ($2$--$70\times$ NVE) but may miss subtler forms of value distortion that emerge at different temporal scales or with alternative embedding parameterizations.
tool_args.new_string: Our study has several limiting assumptions. Second, the primary evaluation covers two proprioceptive locomotion environments and one manipulation task (PickCube); generalization to pixel-based observations, Atari, or real-robot deployments remains untested. Third, our causal claims rest on a factorial observational design rather than a formal causal identification strategy; confounds between embedding training dynamics and other optimizer state cannot be fully excluded. Fourth, the NVE $\geq 2.0\times$ threshold achieves perfect classification on $n{=}36$ configurations but has not been validated on held-out architectures or environments. Finally, per-configuration seed counts (4--5 seeds; \citet{colas2018seeds}) are powered to detect large-magnitude CIVO ($2$--$70\times$ NVE) but may miss subtler value distortion at different temporal scales.

13	\paragraph{Practical implications.}
14	For practitioners considering variable-rate imagination in world-model RL, our results suggest three operational guidelines. First, monitor NVE throughout training: a sustained rise above $2.0\times$ after an initial warm-up window reliably indicates CIVO onset and should trigger early stopping or checkpoint rollback before the policy degrades irreversibly. Second, use frozen-embedding runs as a \emph{diagnostic control} during development---if a frozen embedding achieves comparable task performance to its trained counterpart, the trained embedding's additional representational capacity is likely fueling co-adaptation rather than improving temporal reasoning. Third, the failure of all tested post-hoc interventions implies that CIVO must ultimately be addressed at the architectural level, either by decoupling the temporal embedding from the value-prediction pathway or by redesigning the imagination procedure to periodically re-anchor predictions to real-data statistics. The NVE metric itself is lightweight (requiring only the critic's value estimates and episodic returns already tracked during training) and can be integrated into standard logging pipelines at negligible computational cost.

tool_args.old_string: Our study has several limiting assumptions. First, all experiments use a single world-model architecture (DreamerV3's RSSM with discrete latents); we have not verified whether CIVO manifests in transformer-based world models \citep{micheli2023iris}, TD-MPC variants \citep{hansen2024tdmpc2}, or diffusion-based planners. Second, the primary evaluation covers two proprioceptive locomotion environments and one manipulation task (PickCube); generalization to pixel-based observations, Atari, or real-robot deployments remains untested. Third, our causal claims rest on a factorial observational design rather than a formal causal identification strategy; confounds between embedding training dynamics and other optimizer state cannot be fully excluded. Fourth, the NVE $\geq 2.0\times$ threshold achieves perfect classification on $n{=}36$ configurations but has not been validated on held-out architectures or environments.
